security_audit.summary: Most command and script static findings are Markdown examples rather than executable skill code. However, the skill contains actionable offensive guidance for credential phishing, defacement, external exfiltration endpoints, and filter bypass techniques, so publication requires strong restrictions or content changes.

remediation.suggestion: Remove fake login and credential capture forms, or replace them with harmless placeholders that cannot collect secrets.
Use non-routable example domains and state that external collection endpoints must not be deployed during marketplace use.
Reframe defacement content as impact descriptions and use non-destructive visual markers for authorized proof of concept testing.
Limit bypass guidance to defensive validation, add explicit scope controls, and remove event-handler payloads that enable script execution.
Add scope confirmation, rate limits, logging guidance, and warnings before any sample script sends HTTP requests.

content.value_statement: HTML injection can enable phishing, defacement, and misleading page content. This skill helps authorized testers validate impact and document remediation.
actual_capabilities: Explains HTML injection concepts and how they differ from XSS.
Lists common input surfaces such as search, profiles, comments, cookies, and headers.
Shows manual validation workflows for reflected and stored HTML injection.
Describes phishing, defacement, CSS, meta, iframe, and form action impacts.
Includes Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP, and simple fuzzing workflow guidance.
Provides remediation guidance for output encoding, sanitization, validation, and CSP.
limitations: It does not verify authorization or testing scope for the user.
It does not run tools or prove a vulnerability by itself.
Some examples are offensive and should be confined to approved labs.
Manual browser validation is still required for accurate impact assessment.

use_cases.title: Validate an Authorized Finding
use_cases.description: Plan safe steps to confirm whether user input renders as HTML and document reproducible evidence.

use_cases.title: Triage Reported Injection Risk
use_cases.description: Classify stored, reflected, and form-based injection reports before assigning remediation priority.

use_cases.title: Improve Output Handling
use_cases.description: Compare risky rendering patterns with safer escaping, sanitization, and policy controls.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Safe Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment planning for one input field.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this authorized web application, help me plan a safe HTML injection triage for the search field. Include scope checks, non-destructive test ideas, and evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Reflection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate validation of a suspected reflected parameter.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have permission to test a reflected parameter. Build a step-by-step validation plan that avoids credential collection and explains expected browser evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Impact
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report preparation after a confirmed rendering issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these observed results, classify impact across misleading content, links, forms, and defacement. Recommend severity and remediation language for a report.

prompt_templates.title: Review Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this remediation plan for HTML injection. Create a retest checklist covering output encoding, allowed markup, CSP, and stored versus reflected cases.

output_examples.input: A search term appears unescaped in the results page.
output: Likely reflected HTML injection in the search parameter.
Confirm with a harmless visual marker in an authorized browser session.
Recommend context-aware output encoding for the rendered value.

output_examples.input: A profile bio accepts formatting that persists for other users.
output: Potential stored HTML injection with broader user impact.
Assess whether forms, links, or full-page overlays can mislead users.
Recommend an allowlist sanitizer and server-side validation.

output_examples.input: A team has patched an HTML injection report.
output: Retest reflected and stored paths with harmless markers.
Verify encoded output in HTML, attribute, and URL contexts.
Check that CSP and sanitization changes do not break intended formatting.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and rate limits before testing any target.
Use harmless proof markers and avoid collecting credentials or personal data.
Document exact inputs, browser evidence, affected contexts, and remediation guidance.
anti_patterns: Do not test production systems without explicit written permission.
Do not deploy credential capture forms or attacker-controlled endpoints.
Do not treat visual reflection as full XSS without proving script execution.

faq.question: What is HTML injection?
faq.answer: HTML injection occurs when untrusted input is rendered as markup instead of encoded text.

faq.question: Is HTML injection the same as XSS?
faq.answer: No. HTML injection changes page markup, while XSS executes script. HTML injection can still support phishing or defacement.

faq.question: Does this skill run attacks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown workflow with examples. Users must operate tools within authorized scope.

faq.question: What authorization is required?
faq.answer: Use it only with explicit written permission for the application, accounts, data, and testing window.

faq.question: How should evidence be collected?
faq.answer: Use harmless visual markers, screenshots, request details, and affected parameters. Do not capture real credentials.

faq.question: How do teams fix HTML injection?
faq.answer: Apply context-aware output encoding, sanitize allowed markup, validate input, and use CSP as defense in depth.
